utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good afternoon to everyone. Madam Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. Good afternoon, everyone in and around the courtroom. This is case number IT-03-69-T, the Prosecutor versus Jovica Stanisic and Franko Simatovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. I did not hear of any procedural issues to be raised at this moment, which means - and it's a pity for those who are in the public gallery following our proceedings - that we have to move into closed session because we'll hear the remainder of the evidence of the present witness in closed session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar would like to put a correction on the record in relation to the last photograph, the still marked by the witness.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Last exhibit previously marked as P1566 should be P1573, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's on the record. Thank you, Madam Registrar. There's one issue remaining, that is, we'll not sit tomorrow. We'll also not sit next week. We'll not sit on the 25th of October, which is a UN holiday. I would like to briefly discuss with you the days after that, that is, 26th, 27th, 28th, and 29th of October. As matters stand at present and also keeping in mind the concerns you had, Mr. Groome, also keeping in mind the condition of Mr. Stanisic, on the 26th we are scheduled to sit in the afternoon. On the 27th we are scheduled to sit in the afternoon, but for co-ordination purposes the Chamber is intending to sit on that morning. The 28th we are sitting in the afternoon, that's Thursday. And we could also sit and I think I indicated that already earlier, that we might want to sit for four days that week -- on the 29th we could sit in the afternoon. Now, there is a possibility that since Friday afternoon is not the most popular day of the week, that there may still be an opening to move that to Friday morning. But as matters stand at this moment we could only sit on Friday afternoon. Could I hear from the parties whether a schedule sitting 26th afternoon, 27th morning, 28th Thursday afternoon, and 29th Friday in the afternoon, whether that would meet any objections or any problems.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: No objection, obviously subject to Mr. Stanisic's health.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We have no objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Jordash, you raised Mr. Stanisic's health. You know that we intended to move slowly to three and then four days. As far as the medical reports are concerned, until now there seems not to be a firm obstacle against sitting four days a week. Not to say that we would change that if there are special circumstances raised by Mr. Groome matters to consider to sit in that week four days. We will -- it's most likely that we will be able, especially in view of what -- the positions taken by the parties, that we'll be able to follow that schedule for that week. Then we adjourn and we'll not sit next week. We'll resume on Tuesday, the 26th of October, quarter past 2.00 in the afternoon, as far as matters stand now, in Courtroom I.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 26th day of October, 2010, at 2.15 p.m. 23 24 25

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 6.41 p.m.,
